precepts.text: Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law? That is what they do: they work mischief and then call it law. Think about the laws framed against us since this administration came into office.
precepts.point: In closing: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt. That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
He that worketh mischief: that is what they do. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” They work mischief and then call it law.

Two men getting married, two women getting married: all of these laws. Think about what Trump has done since he came into office: all of the firing and all the DEI hires, all of this is against us. They frame mischief and call it law.

A throne of iniquity cannot have fellowship with God. The ruler that frames mischief by a law over another man is ruling to his own hurt, and the mischief he works shall fall upon him.

precepts.text: I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first. God shall be known in his judgments: when we sin and find ourselves back in captivity and prison houses, his judgment stands, and his prophecies are fulfilled. Take heed and fear God.
precepts.point: Your calling is not to be a slave; your nine to five is for you to keep these commandments, to remember that you are called and requested of God to magnify his law upon the earth. We must obey the laws of God and the just laws of the land so we do not get caught up in the oppression. Some need to be locked up if they rob and steal; but what we institute is the keeping of God's commandments so you stay far from all of that.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?
precepts.point: Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you live, you still have it.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.text: Woe to them that devise iniquity; when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.
precepts.point: They covet fields and take them by violence; they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” They do not abandon the law; they weaponise it. They wrote the laws, so they know how to get around them. The most powerful pen in the world, with a stack of bills beside it, is the president of the United States, and every nation bends the knee. Violence gets reframed legally in their decrees and doctrines: kidnapping becomes a law enforcement operation, sanctions become international order, theft becomes stabilising the region. When he promised to lock up the criminal illegal immigrants, you thought thieves and murderers; but by their law, anyone here without papers is a criminal. That is framing mischief by a law.

Micah shows how they work: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” When the morning is light means in broad daylight, because they can frame it by law, and he says his own morality is the only limit. It is in the power of their hand because they are after the working of Satan, given authority to set kings up and take them down.

“And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” It is not just the resources; they want the identity too. Venezuela's vice president said the country was attacked by Zionists seeking to enslave the nation. Netanyahu, whom he calls his boss, visited before the attack. Machado, who won the Nobel Peace Prize and then gave it to Trump, promised to open the oil to their companies and move Venezuela's embassy to Jerusalem, because everybody has to bow the knee to the impostors.

Maduro said he is a Jew in his blood, from the twelve tribes, and that the man over there is not a real Jew. That is the heritage they are after. The ADL says it has analysts monitoring 24 hours a day and trains law enforcement, and in Patagonia Israeli tourists were caught setting fires in a protected preserve they cannot buy unless it is damaged. Their eye is on the land and on the lost tribes. They practise it in the light, because it is in the power of their hand.

precepts.text: The throne of iniquity, which frameth mischief by a law.
precepts.point: They covet fields and take them by violence, and oppress a man and his house.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
When the morning is light they practise it, and they do it through law. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?”

That is how the whole system was designed. The Constitution was not framed for us; we were three-fifths of a man. It was based on Roman and Greek democracy, which you read of in the Maccabees, and even then we were not part of it. It was framed to keep them in power. The Supreme Court interprets Esau's constitution, and it is all set up with words that frame mischief to benefit them. Our salvation is not in that.

Look at it now: the Supreme Court, 6 to 3, on its shadow docket, behind closed doors, gave ICE the green light to stop and detain people based on appearance, language, accent or workplace. That is racial profiling blessed by law, and it targets the northern kingdom. So if you are a citizen and you fit the profile, carry your passport or a passport card.

Sanctions, asset seizures, blockades: all of that is violence too, economic violence. When you oppress a man and his house and his heritage, whether you take him by the neck or frame a law, it is still violence. If what they want is not legal, they find a way to weaponize the legal system. That is the throne of iniquity.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? That is the spirit the Most High looks for, one who will stand up for his people against the workers of iniquity; he is not worried about outward appearance.
precepts.point: This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David's brothers: they were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David rose early, left the sheep with a keeper, and came to the trench as the host was shouting for the battle. While he saluted his brethren, the champion came up “and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.” The same daily smack talk.

“And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.” Think on it: the whole nation’s freedom, everything they possessed, was on the line, and they ran scared. This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David’s brothers. They were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled.

“Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” That is the spirit the Most High looks for, one who will stand up for his people against the workers of iniquity. He is not worried about outward appearance.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers, or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?
precepts.point: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and have not called upon God? Our people get swallowed up by the other nations.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge? who eat up my people as they eat bread”. Our people get swallowed up by the other nations. Psalm 94 asks the question that goes with it: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” The workers of iniquity eat up the Most High's people as they eat bread, and the call is for someone to rise up and stand up against them.

precepts.text: The unjust judge avenged the widow for her continual coming; how much more shall God avenge His own elect speedily, yet shall He find faith on earth when the Son of man cometh.
precepts.point: We ask the question, how long shall the wicked triumph.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“O Lord God, to whom vengeance belongeth; O God, to whom vengeance belongeth, shew thyself.” We really have to understand this in these times when a lot of our brothers and sisters want to take up arms against the oppressor, because vengeance belongeth to the Most High. Christ gave the parable: “There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.”

The unjust judge avenged the widow for her continual coming. “And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily.” How much more shall God avenge his own elect who cry day and night unto him, even though he bear long with them.

That is the answer to “how long shall the wicked triumph?” We keep crying to him like the widow, and he will avenge speedily. But Christ ends with the warning: “Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?” Shall he find faith on earth when the Son of man comes, or will we have taken up arms and stopped waiting on him?

precepts.text: In your patience possess your souls; while we cry out how long, do not lose faith, Israel.
precepts.point: We ask the question, how long shall the wicked triumph.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
While we cry out “how long shall the wicked triumph?”, Christ tells us how to wait: “In your patience possess ye your souls.”

In your patience possess your souls. Vengeance belongs to the Most High, not to us, so while we ask how long, do not lose faith, Israel. The patience is the possessing of your soul; take up patience, not arms, until he shows himself and renders a reward to the proud.

precepts.text: We are the Most High's battle axe and weapons of war, so we must prepare ourselves to be part of that army.
precepts.point: Yet they say the Lord shall not see, neither shall the God of Jacob regard it. That is a heavy point, because it shows the people know who we are; it does not say the God of all people, it says the God of Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“They break in pieces thy people, O Lord, and afflict thine heritage. They slay the widow and the stranger, and murder the fatherless.” That is the curses we are up under. The workers of iniquity boast themselves, like Trump and the Proud Boys who can scale the walls and get into the White House, while a sister who did a U-turn out there got shot up. Do not think the Most High is negligent or does not see these things.

The Lord turns it around in Jeremiah: “Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms”. They break his people in pieces now, but we are the Most High's battle axe and weapons of war, and with us he will break in pieces the nations and destroy kingdoms.

So we must prepare ourselves to be part of that army. And notice they say “neither shall the God of Jacob regard it.” That is a heavy point, because it shows the people know who we are; it does not say the God of all people, it says the God of Jacob.

precepts.text: The Most High scattered us into corners as a curse, but feared the wrath of the enemy lest they should say their hand is high; He knows the heathen are a nation void of counsel.
precepts.point: The Most High knoweth the thoughts of man that they are vanity. He knows our thoughts as His heritage, and He knows the thoughts of the heathen because He created them.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“The Lord knoweth the thoughts of man, that they are vanity.” He knows our thoughts as his heritage, and he knows the thoughts of the heathen because he created them. Moses shows him weighing both: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men: Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy, lest their adversaries should behave themselves strangely, and lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this.”

The Most High scattered us into corners as a curse, but he feared the wrath of the enemy, lest they should say their hand is high and the Lord has not done all this. He knows what the heathen would think. “For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them.” He knows the heathen are a nation void of counsel.

That is why the psalm says “Understand, ye brutish among the people: and ye fools, when will ye be wise?” He that planted the ear shall hear and he that formed the eye shall see, and he that teaches man knowledge knows the vain thoughts of the nations who think their own hand did this to Israel.

precepts.text: Paul says God hath not cast away His people whom He foreknew, for Paul himself is an Israelite of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
precepts.point: The Most High will not cast off His people nor forsake His inheritance. People say black people are gentiles and nationality is not important, but this tells you nationality is extremely important; you must know who you are.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will not cast off his people, neither will he forsake his inheritance.” Paul asks the question straight: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

Paul says God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, and his proof is himself: an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. He knew his nationality and his tribe. He goes on to Elias, who “maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life”, and still God had not cast them off.

People say black people are gentiles and nationality is not important, but this tells you nationality is extremely important; you must know who you are. Blessed is the man whom the Most High chastens and teaches out of his law; that is why in Revelation the books are opened and the book of your life is measured against the laws. He chastens his people, but he does not cast them off.

precepts.text: Iniquity, spoiling, and violence are before us; the law is slack and judgment never goes forth, and wrong judgment proceeds so our oppressors are found not guilty.
precepts.point: The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” A throne is the image of power, so shall that power have fellowship with the Most High, which frames mischief by law? Habakkuk saw the same throne: “Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention. Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.”

Iniquity, spoiling and violence are before us. The law is slack and judgment never goes forth, and wrong judgment proceeds, so our oppressors are found not guilty. That is mischief framed by a law.

The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want. The wicked compass about the righteous, and the throne that does it has no fellowship with the Most High.

precepts.text: Be ye not unequally yoked with unbelievers, for there is no fellowship between righteousness and unrighteousness, nor concord between Christ and Belial.
precepts.point: The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
The throne of iniquity shall have no fellowship with the Most High, and neither should we have fellowship with it. “Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?”

Be ye not unequally yoked with unbelievers, for there is no fellowship between righteousness and unrighteousness, nor concord between Christ and Belial. The same word, fellowship, that Psalm 94 asks about the throne that frames mischief by law is the word Paul uses for us.

If the power that makes men marry men and sets the new year in the midst of winter has no fellowship with God, then he that believes has no part with it either.

precepts.text: He that provides not for his own house hath denied the faith and is worse than an infidel, so do not hang around a slothful man or woman.
precepts.point: The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
Paul asks what part he that believeth has with an infidel, and then shows who the infidel is among us: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

He that provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel. So do not hang around a slothful man or woman. The throne of iniquity that frames mischief by a law has no fellowship with the Most High, and the one who will not provide for his own house is worse than the unbeliever we are told not to be yoked with.

precepts.text: We are the temple of the living God; He does not say He is the God of all people, so come out from among them, be ye separate, and touch not the unclean thing.
precepts.point: The mischief framed by law is men marrying men, women marrying women, setting the new year in the midst of winter to have us worshiping another god, and coexist meaning you can serve any gods you want.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” We are the temple of the living God. Notice he does not say he is the God of all people; he says I will be their God and they shall be my people.

“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. Come out from among them, be ye separate, and touch not the unclean thing.

That is the answer to Psalm 94:20. The throne that frames mischief by a law, men marrying men, the new year set in the midst of winter, coexist with any god you want, has no fellowship with the Most High, so his temple comes out from among it and is separate, and he receives us.

precepts.text: For the same purpose the Most High raised up Pharaoh, that He might show His power in him and that His name might be declared throughout all the earth.
precepts.point: But the Most High is my defense and the rock of my refuge, and He shall bring upon them their own iniquity and cut them off in their own wickedness. The first verse says vengeance is His, and the last verse says He shall cut them off; we do not have the power ourselves.

note.label: Psalm 94: The God of Vengeance and Defense of His People

precepts.why:
“And he shall bring upon them their own iniquity, and shall cut them off in their own wickedness; yea, the Lord our God shall cut them off.” They gather against the soul of the righteous and condemn the innocent blood; this has been happening to us from the beginning, especially in Babylon. But the Most High is our defence and the rock of our refuge, and he does the cutting off.

Pharaoh shows how he uses even the wicked for that: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.”

For the same purpose the Most High raised up Pharaoh, that he might show his power in him and that his name might be declared throughout all the earth. The wicked are raised up so that the Lord can bring their own iniquity upon them. The first verse of the psalm says vengeance is his, and the last verse says he shall cut them off; we do not have the power ourselves.

precepts.text: Who will rise up for me against the evildoers; Phinehas rose up.
precepts.point: Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” Phinehas rose up.

When Israel had joined themselves unto Baal–peor and the plague was breaking in upon them, “Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.” He answered the question of Psalm 94 with action, and it was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations.

precepts.text: The throne of iniquity frameth mischief by a law and gathers against the soul of the righteous to condemn innocent blood, but the Most High is our defense.
precepts.point: They had almost consumed me upon earth, but I forsook not Thy precepts. Quicken me after Thy lovingkindness, so shall I keep the testimony of Thy mouth. The mischief is framed by law, giving rights to sodomites and signing all kinds of wickedness, but the Most High is our defense.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The pits are traps set by the proud. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law? They gather themselves together against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.”

The throne of iniquity is America, the pinnacle of sin, where once you go out your doors sin is everywhere. It frames mischief by a law, giving rights to sodomites and signing all kinds of wickedness, and gathers against the soul of the righteous to condemn innocent blood. Are you going to have fellowship with that? The answer should be no.

They had almost consumed us upon earth, but the Most High is our defense, and we forsake not his precepts.

precepts.text: Who will rise up against the evildoers and stand up against the workers of iniquity, which is the hedge and the gap of one who would turn the Lord's wrath from the people.
precepts.point: He sought for a man to make up the hedge and stand in the gap before Him so He would not destroy the land, but He found none, so He poured out His indignation and consumed them with the fire of His wrath.

note.label: Ezekiel 22: The Bloody City

precepts.why:
“I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.” The psalm asks the same question: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?”

That is the hedge and the gap. The one who would turn the Lord's wrath from the people is the one who rises up against the evildoers and stands up against the workers of iniquity. And look who the workers of iniquity were: her prophets in a conspiracy “like a roaring lion ravening the prey”, devouring souls and making many widows; her priests who violated His law and “put no difference between the holy and profane”, hiding their eyes from His sabbaths; her princes “like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain”; prophets daubing them with untempered morter, saying “Thus saith the Lord God, when the Lord hath not spoken”; and the people of the land using oppression, robbery and vexing the poor and needy and the stranger. The leaders of Israel were very corrupt, and the same oppression, robbery and extortion ran through the leadership.

It is just like today, where our people put no difference between anything, and it is called Christianity. Nobody rose up against the evildoers, He found none, so He poured out His indignation and consumed them with the fire of His wrath, recompensing their own way upon their heads.
